title: QSOL UFF v5.3.0: Nonclaim Calibration and Evidence-Scope Discipline for Reproducible Astrophysics
description:
QSOL UFF v5.3.0 is an additive epistemic-assurance release of the reproducible astrophysics and falsification laboratory. It retains the v5.2.0 scientific implementation, defense-in-depth evidence workflow, and Lean 4 formal assurance layer while adding a reusable nonclaim calibration vocabulary and a machine-readable worked reference.

The v5.3.0 calibration rule is EXISTENCE != ROBUSTNESS != GENERICITY != PREVALENCE != EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT != PHYSICAL_TRUTH. The release records forbidden promotions such as can form -> likely to form, fine-tuned success -> robust success, constructed trajectory -> generic outcome, and theoretical possibility -> empirical occurrence.

The worked reference is Jampolski & Rezzolla, Formation of gravastars, arXiv:2509.15302v2. It is included as a claim-scope calibration source because the paper demonstrates gravastar formation under fine-tuned conditions while leaving robustness under more realistic assumptions and the relative likelihood of gravastar versus black-hole formation open.

Scientific boundary: the reference is not evidence that astrophysical gravastars are generic, common, observed, or physically preferred. The existing UFF rule REPLAY_VERIFIED != ENSEMBLE_CALIBRATED != PHYSICAL_TRUTH remains unchanged.
